description: List your Router payments: the unified ledger across every service and delegation, newest first, at most 1000 records. Each record carries its `id` (the `paymentId` get_payment_result takes), `createdAt`, `status`, `protocol`, `network`, `requestId`, `delegationId` and `amount` in the asset's smallest unit (see `assetDecimals`), not in cents. Each row also carries `deliveryStatus`: `delivered` (request settled), `charged_not_delivered` (request failed and the merchant charge was observed), `charged_unconfirmed` (charge observed; delivery unconfirmed), `not_charged` (reconciliation recorded no merchant charge, including unreadable write-offs; not conclusive proof that no money moved), `not_delivered` (the merchant answered with an error, so nothing was delivered, and no charge has been seen: the amount stays reserved until reconciliation decides, after confirmed cancellation or payment authorization expiry, whether the merchant charged; it is not a confirmed charge), or `pending` (charge outcome unknown). Issued + `pending` means the charge outcome is unknown: neither payment nor no charge is established. On SPT and card rails, pending is not proof of no charge; those rows are never decided on chain. `merchantSettlementObservedAt` records an observed merchant charge; null is not, on its own, proof of no charge. Flag both charged states to the user. Each record also carries `fundingSource`, the funding it used: `delegation`, or `subscription` for your Nevermined credits, with or without a subscription. On a `subscription` row, `deliveryStatus` and `merchantSettlementObservedAt` describe what Nevermined paid the merchant, not a charge to you: what the call cost you is `creditsCharged`, and `creditsStatus` says whether that stands (`Committed` spent, `Reserved` held or marked for refund, `Refunded` returned). Do not report a charged state on such a row as a charge to the user. Pass `requestId` to look up the one payment with that id: the answer is then `{"presence":…,"payments":[…]}`, it ignores the other filters and the 1000-record limit, and `presence: "absent"` means no payment carries that id. Use this tool to reconcile an uncertain payment or find a paymentId; it does not return service responses (use get_payment_result) or the remaining budget (use get_budget, whose figures include fees and rounding). Reading costs nothing. Requires your Nevermined API key on the Authorization header.

delegationId.description: Only payments charged to this delegation.

from.description: ISO-8601 lower bound on `createdAt`, inclusive. An unparseable value is an error.

requestId.description: The `requestId` a pay_service or route_by_intent result gave you, matched exactly. Finds that one payment wherever it sits in the ledger; the other filters are ignored.

to.description: ISO-8601 upper bound on `createdAt`, inclusive. An unparseable value is an error.

name: list_payments
title: List payments
